name: Hookline Independent Freight Day Haul Kit
description:
Not corponation-issued — this is the uniform of a self-employed dock and freight hauler working Hookline's independent operator network. The centerpiece is a heavy canvas work shirt in faded rust-brown with pearl-snap closures, the left chest pocket bearing a hand-stitched Hookline patch in white and orange — a stylized anchor over a circuit node. The sleeves are rolled to the elbows and secured with canvas tab-buttons. Beneath it, a plain white moisture-wick tank is visible at the collar. Over the shirt goes a multi-pocket tool vest in safety orange with deep cargo pockets, a map-fold document slot, and a clipped utility carabiner at the left hip carrying a ring of dock access fobs. The vest's right shoulder panel has a clear ID badge window.

The trousers are Goretek HaulMaster Cargos in dark charcoal — reinforced knees, wide thigh cargo pockets sealed with hook-and-loop closures, and a double-layered seat. A wide leather-analog belt with a heavy roller buckle cinches the waist. Footwear is the Dockmaster Deepwade Boot — waterproof, composite-toed, with aggressive lug soles for wet dock surfaces. The boots are salt-stained and scuffed but the soles are unworn. A battered wide-brim synth-canvas hat in faded khaki keeps acid-rain drizzle off the face. On chrome-armed haulers, the right sleeve of the work shirt is removed and replaced with a reinforced aug-channel strap that secures the vest across the shoulder.
functionality: Multi-pocket tool vest with document storage and ID window, dock access fob ring, waterproof composite-toe footwear for wet surfaces, aug-channel sleeve modification for chrome arm compatibility, acid-rain resistant hat, heavy-duty cargo storage throughout
what_it_says: Independent. Not owned by a corponation roster, not drawing a subsidized wage, not subject to a uniform demerit system. The Hookline patch is a network affiliation, not an employer brand — this person chose it. The worn boots and salt-stained brim say real hours on real docks. The hand-stitched patch says they care enough about the work to mark it.
worn_by: gig-economy port laborers working Circuit-tier docks
manufacturer: Hookline Independent Operators Network (patch and vest); Goretek (trousers); mixed independent sourcing
story_hooks: The document slot in the vest contains a manifest that does not match the cargo currently on the dock — and the hauler swears they were handed it sealed.
A Hookline operator in this kit is the last person confirmed to have handled a container that has since gone missing from the port's tracking system.
The dock access fobs on the hip ring include one that should not exist — a code for a berth that officially closed two years ago.
